Cat Power is the recording/performing moniker of American singer-songwriter Chan Marshall, born 21 January 1972 in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.

Initially the name of Marshall's first band in Atlanta in the early 90s, "Cat Power" has since served as her stage name.

RAYE is a Grammy-winning English singer and songwriter from London. She is best known for her break-out hit 'Escapism.' (2023) and her international smash hit 'Where Is My Husband!' (2025). Following the release of her self-released album 'My 21st Century Blues' (2023) she broke the record for the artist with wins in the most categories in a single year at the Brit Awards (2024).

American jazz pianist, composer and leader of his eponymous orchestra (born April 29, 1899, Washington, D.C.; died May 24, 1974 in New York City, N.Y.).
Known for his residency at the [l=Cotton Club] (1927-1931) and for composing over a thousand pieces (often in collaboration), many of them now standards. [a258464] shared composing duties (1939-1967). 
Father of [a323069], who took over the leadership of the orchestra after Duke died remaining until his own death in 1996. Grandfather of [a5641533].

Saba (stylized as SABA), is an American rapper, songwriter and record producer, born 17 July 1994 in Chicago, Illinois. He grew up in the Austin neighborhood of the West Side of Chicago.
One of the earliest producers of footwork and juke. Active as a DJ since the early 90s. Based in Chicago.

One of the most bizarre, funny, and extremely skillful American hip-hop acts, Brooklyn-based Fu-Schnickens erupted in 1992 with their highly acclaimed single, "Ring The Alarm," an update of the reggae tune from [a=Tenor Saw]. Their equally heralded debut album filled with many references to martial arts and Asian culture predating the [a=Wu-Tang Clan], "F.U.: Don't Take It Personal," contained the hits "True Fuschnick," "Movie Scene," and "La Schmoove," (Featuring [a=Phife Dawg] from [a=A Tribe Called Quest]).  The later collaboration gave them status as an affiliate crew of the revered [a=Native Tongues] collective.  
In 1993, Poc-Fu, Moc-Fu, and Chip-Fu returned with a Top 40 single, "What's Up Doc ?" featuring the NBA star [a=Shaquille O'Neal], who had praised the group as his favorite. The lead single for Shaq's debut, [a=Shaq Diesel], and their following album, "Nervous Breakdown" (1994), also garnered the bangers "Breakdown" and "Sum Dum Monkey."  Fu-Schnickens made the amicable decision to part ways in 1996 to pursue individual creative endeavors.

Label Code: LC 0392 / LC 00392.

Founded in 1958 by Jack Warner as a soundtrack factory for Warner Bros. movie studios, Warner Bros. Records and its family of subsidiary labels, which includes Reprise Records, Sire Records, Maverick Records, Warner Nashville, Warner Jazz, Warner Western, and Word Label Group encompassed a full spectrum of musical genres.
After more than 60 years using the Warner Bros. name and logo (and following the end of a 15-year licensing agreement with AT&T/WarnerMedia, until 2018 Time Warner), the label was rebranded in May 2019 to simply [l=Warner Records].

Warner Bros. is known to have used various companies pressing facilities, including but not limited to, [l376197] and [l403953].

Label designs:
Mono LPs:
- 1958-62 - Grey label, black WB Shield and black 33 1/3 at bottom outlined in yellow.
- 1962-66 - Grey label, black WB Shield and black 33 1/3 at bottom outlined in white.
- 1966-67 - Gold Label, MONAURAL at bottom.

Stereo LPs:
- 1958-65 - Gold label with VITAPHONIC LONG PLAY at bottom
- 1965-67 - Gold label, VITAPHONIC wording deleted; boxed STEREO at bottom.
- 1967-January, 1970 - Green Label, Warner Bros. - Seven Arts Records at top, with W7 logo beneath it. (After February the "W7" was replaced by the WB shield, but some Columbia plants had W7 labels they "burned off" well into the summer.)
- February, 1970-73 - Green Label, Warner Bros. Records at top, with WB Shield underneath it.
- April 1973, Q2-1975, Q3 - Burbank Palm Trees label with WB Shield at top without "Records" banner, introduced March/April 1973. No mention of Warner Communications in rimtext.
- 1975, Q3-1978, Q3 - Burbank Palm Trees label with WB Shield at top, with "Records" banner. Warner Communications wording and WCI logo in rimtext.
- 91505 zip code in rimtext used from 1974 - 1977 (Columbia Pressings)
- 91510 zip code in rimtext used beginning 1976 (Capitol Pressings)
- 1978, Q3-1983, Q1 - Tan label w/ narrow horizontal lines
- 1983+ - White label, large WB shield at top and "ghosted" gray shields floating in the background.

Information about how to determine first pressings of US LPs on this label:
Grey label, black WB Shield, WB in gold print # 1200 - approx. 1470
Same, but in white print # 1470 - 1615
Gold Label # 1616 - 1737 (last spotted gold label)
Green Label, Warner Bros. - Seven Arts Records, W7 logo # 1738 - 1834
Green Label, Warner Bros. Records. w/ WB Shield # 1835 - 2694 (last spotted green label)
Palm Trees Label NO ADDRESS at bottom # 2693 - 2865
Saul Bass W logo on label rim and sleeves are 1975 or later.
Palm Trees Label 3300 Warner Blvd. # 2866 - 3180
Dark Cream Label w/Tan horizontal lines and address in perimeter since1978  # 3181 - up to 1982/1983
Light Cream (Off-white) Label w/no lines and w/Ghost WB logo's in the background - everything since 1983

~ Please note: A few select "WB" LPs pressed in 1983 also were issue with the pinstripe (previous) label [r=925017] as the 'ghost logos' were being introduced during the label design change.  Releases with BSK and having 'ghost logos' labels should be considered a "reissue or repress" as they kept the same release # from the original 1970s #s but changed the label to the new version.

An example of label versions during the change:
[r=4825085]

Source: Joe Lindsay's ''Record Label Guide'' and Raymond Dumont's collection.

This is not part of the catalogue number and should not be entered as such. Instead, it's a label identification code and may be entered in the Barcode and Other Identifiers fields in Other.

Please note, some Mute issues also carry an EMI logo. This is not a label and EMI should not be added as a label, it instead indicates that Mute was part of the EMI Group.

Founded in 1978 by [a=Daniel Miller], Mute (also known as [l36339]) releases various forms of music, with an emphasis on electronic and experimental pop. In May 2002 the label was acquired by the [l=EMI Group]. In 2010 Miller did an agreement with EMI to handle Mute as an independent label again, licensing the trademark from EMI via his company [l=Mute Artists Ltd.], but EMI kept the rights over Mute's back catalogue. After the EMI Group was dissolved, in 2012 [l206061] acquired [l636]'s back catalogue.

Branch offices exist in Germany ([l168349]) and in North America ([l36296]). 

Mute has spawned many regional and special-interest sublabels, some of which are still active. One offshoot, [l=Parallel Series], even became independent of [l636] Mute also operates Mute Bank Mail Order, which sells the label's merchandise directly to consumers. Mute Bank published two issues of [i]Mute Statement[/i], a softcover book that details the entire discography of the label and includes band profiles and photos of release artwork.

Another label strongly associated with Mute is [l=Toast Hawaii], run by [a=Depeche Mode]'s [a=Andrew Fletcher].

profile.profile:
American independent record label founded 1997 or 1998 by Canadian attorney [a=Cameron Strang], currently based in Nashville, Tennessee, and Athens, Georgia.
International label code: LC 52772.

Features a rock-oriented (alt, indie, country, folk, Americana, etc.) roster. Exclusively represented PBS Television program [l=Austin City Limits] to release both archival and current performances via [l=Live From Austin TX].

Originally founded in Minneapolis, Minnesota (from Strang's and [a=Kelley Deal]'s [l=Nice Records (2)]); relocated to Los Angeles, California, in November 1998; Austin, Texas, office opened March 2000 (via merger with [a=George Fontaine Sr.]'s [l=Doolittle Records]); Athens, Georgia, office opened 2010, Nashville, Tennessee, office opened 2014.

Initially distributed in the U.S. by RED Music; Alternative Distribution Alliance (ADA) in 2013; later in the U.S. by Redeye Distribution (2018); and internationally by PIAS Group.

Acquired Texas Music Group, including the [l=Antone's Records] and [l=Watermelon Records] labels, in 2010; launched [l=Normaltown Records] imprint in 2012.

The label was co-owned by Strang and president [a=George Fontaine Sr.], until Strang departed in 2011; John Allen was appointed president of the label in 2014.

For unofficial/bootleg releases purporting to be from this label, please use [l=New West Records (2)].

ユニバーサル　インターナショナル in Japanese.
Universal International is a division of the Japanese record company Universal Music K.K. It handles Universal's international labels like Geffen, A&M Records and Interscope for the Japanese market.

Releases issued by Universal International carry branding of one of Universal's international labels. The catalogue numbers of these releases start with 'UI'.

Note: This is a company/division, do not enter it as a label. Add it as a company, with relevant company role as shown on release. If no role is specified on release, add it as record company.

Please add the branded multi-national label as a label.
